Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-transcribe-medium-0132-reverse-02", "row_sha256": "083a2dfde099cfa38a52f0bbce0a8f3d43b8d7d7780ab68ac4f4ab387b4979a1", "mode": "/transcribe", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Remove true hesitation and accidental restarts. Apply explicit corrections to the final stated intent. Preserve meaningful filler-like words and unfinished thoughts. Apply clearly spoken punctuation and list cues. Keep the supplied language.", "input": "the cedar ridge seed exchange met in the grange hall on saturday morning after rain had delayed the outdoor tables. mara lewis brought three trays of scarlet runner beans, a paper sack of calendula seeds, and a notebook with last year's germination notes. joel at the welcome desk checked the receipts and said the room fee and table rental came to $121.58 not $69.31. he pointed to the handwritten total because an earlier draft of the notice had the lower figure beside the wrong event. mara asked whether the posted amount included the two extra folding tables and the cleaning charge and joel said it did. the exchange had six neighborhood growers and about twenty visitors before noon. people traded seed envelopes by variety and wrote the harvest year on small labels so the packets would not be confused later. a grower named ines left instructions for keeping the bean seeds dry and asked mara to save one envelope for the library garden. at closing time the volunteers put the unused labels and pencils in a blue tin, stacked the chairs near the side door, and left the signed receipt in the hall office. joel said he would send a copy of the corrected notice to the growers that afternoon. mara took the notebook home and planned to compare the seed notes with the planting dates in her garden log.", "output": "The Cedar Ridge Seed Exchange met in the grange hall on Saturday morning after rain had delayed the outdoor tables. Mara Lewis brought three trays of scarlet runner beans, a paper sack of calendula seeds, and a notebook with last year's germination notes. Joel at the welcome desk checked the receipts and said the room fee and table rental came to $121.58, not $69.31. He pointed to the handwritten total because an earlier draft of the notice had the lower figure beside the wrong event. Mara asked whether the posted amount included the two extra folding tables and the cleaning charge, and Joel said it did. The exchange had six neighborhood growers and about twenty visitors before noon. People traded seed envelopes by variety and wrote the harvest year on small labels so the packets would not be confused later. A grower named Ines left instructions for keeping the bean seeds dry and asked Mara to save one envelope for the library garden. At closing time, the volunteers put the unused labels and pencils in a blue tin, stacked the chairs near the side door, and left the signed receipt in the hall office. Joel said he would send a copy of the corrected notice to the growers that afternoon. Mara took the notebook home and planned to compare the seed notes with the planting dates in her garden log."}]
